source.title: OpenSimRoot: widening the scope and application of root architectural models
source.license: Creative Commons Attribution License (article license verified in PMC publication record; version not asserted)

claims.claim: The framework grows a connected root network using rules for root initiation, elongation, and direction, with distinct root classes.
claims.location: Materials and Methods → Description of the various modules → Root growth and RSA; Figure 2

claims.claim: Carbon available for growth is compared with carbon requirements; some allocation priorities are pragmatic rather than established physiological mechanisms.
claims.location: Materials and Methods → Carbon allocation to roots

claims.claim: The hydrology module couples soil water transport, a root xylem network, and evapotranspiration, and can simulate compensatory uptake and redistribution.
The hydrology module described in the 2017 article does not simulate drought-related growth responses.
claims.location: Materials and Methods → Hydrology, final sentence

claims.claim: A local nutrient-dependent branching demonstration concentrates branches in phosphorus-rich topsoil and has fewer, longer laterals below.
claims.location: Materials and Methods → Root growth plasticity; Figure 5 caption
claims.evidence_type: Simulation demonstration, not universal crop response

claims.claim: The paper reconstructs an imaged maize root system and predicts nitrate depletion around an imaged wheat root system; about 8% of visible maize roots were omitted because of image segmentation limits.
claims.location: Results → OpenSimRoot as an extension to plant phenotyping; Figure 6

claims.claim: The authors emphasize heuristic value, development and testing of concepts, and prediction of mechanisms and trends.
claims.location: Discussion, paragraph beginning “We regard the heuristic value...”

limits: Original methods/model-development work; earlier SimRoot results in its Results section must not be mislabeled new field findings.
2017 water module lacks drought-related growth feedback.
Shoot architecture is simplified; carbon-allocation priorities partly pragmatic; local responses do not implement gradient sensing.
Image-derived geometries include segmentation and missing-fine-root uncertainties.
No sorghum experiment and no CPlantBox/DuMuX test in the primary source.
inference_for_user: Use the paper’s architecture/function separation and measured-geometry approach to design new sorghum CPlantBox/DuMuX comparisons. Do not transfer crop parameters without sorghum measurements.
copyright_basis: CC Attribution article license explicitly verified in original PMC record; all lesson prose is newly written.
